content_sections.title: 1. Two vowels (8 min)
content_sections.body_text: Live has /ɪ/. Leave has /iː/. For /ɪ/, relax your tongue. For /iː/, move it higher and forward; the sound is often longer too. Say live–leave five times. Change the mouth shape and the length, not only the length.

content_sections.title: 2. Clear repair (8 min)
content_sections.body_text: B: ‘I live here.’ A: ‘Did you say leave?’ B: ‘No, live—/lɪv/.’ A: ‘Oh, you live here.’ Read both roles. Cover the lines and say them again. The question is clear, and B repeats the word that A heard wrongly.

content_sections.title: 3. Two kinds of check (10 min)
content_sections.body_text: For listening, use text-to-speech only to play a hidden order of live and leave; write L or E, then reveal the order. TTS speaks to you; it does not hear your speech. For speaking, say one word without showing it to an independent listener or a speech-recognition tool that displays the word it recognizes. If neither route is available, write ‘not checked.’ Your own replay is practice, not proof.

content_sections.title: 4. Take turns (9 min)
content_sections.body_text: Make a four-line talk like the model: give one fact, hear one word wrongly, ask ‘Did you say …?’, then correct it. Speak both roles with a pause for each reply. Success: the reply answers the question and an independent listener or suitable speech-recognition tool identifies live or leave. If that check is unavailable, mark ‘not checked’ and keep the recording as practice only.
